title: Signature Shuffler-model aggregation
description: Signature edition: The shuffle model sits between local and central DP: clients send locally-randomized reports through a shuffler that strips identifiers and permutes them. Shuffling amplifies privacy — weaker local noise achieves strong central-like guarantees. The ESA (encode-shuffle-analyze) architecture makes it deployable.
method: Clients randomize lightly; the shuffler permutes and de-identifies; the analyzer sees an anonymous multiset; privacy amplifies.
usage: Use to get central-like utility with local-like trust; distribute the shuffler to reduce trust.

demo.code:
print('1M reports -> shuffler permutes, strips IPs')
print('analyzer: anonymous multiset; privacy amplified 10x vs local alone')

title: Signature Secure aggregation (federated)
description: Signature edition: Secure aggregation (Bonawitz et al.) lets a server learn the sum of client values without seeing any individual one — masked contributions cancel out in aggregate. Federated learning uses it: the server improves the model from millions of phones while each phone's update stays private.
method: Clients mask updates with pairwise secrets; the server sums masked values; masks cancel; the server learns only the sum.
usage: Use for federated analytics/ML; handle dropouts (the protocol's hard part).

demo.code:
print('1M phones: masked gradient updates -> server sums')
print('server learns: aggregate gradient (no individual update visible)')

title: Signature Aggregation service design
description: Signature edition: The collector architecture matters: separate ingestion (authenticated but immediately de-identified) from analysis (sees only aggregates), with retention limits between. Defense in depth for telemetry — even a compromised analyzer finds only aggregates, and raw reports auto-expire.
method: Ingest -> de-identify -> aggregate -> expire raw; the analyzer never sees raw reports; retention enforced automatically.
usage: Enforce the split architecturally (different services, different credentials); expire raw data aggressively.

demo.code:
print('ingest: 1M reports -> de-identified in 1h -> raw EXPIRED')
print('analyzer: aggregates only (raw unrecoverable)')

title: Signature Telemetry data minimization
description: Signature edition: Collect the minimum that answers the question: crash stacks yes, full memory dumps no; feature usage counts yes, keystroke logs never. Minimization review precedes every new telemetry field — the cheapest privacy is data never collected.
method: Justify each field; prefer aggregates over raw; review new fields; expire aggressively.
usage: Challenge every new field; 'might be useful someday' is not a justification.

demo.code:
print('proposal: collect full URLs -> REJECTED (paths may contain tokens)')
print('approved: collect domain + status code (sufficient for the question)')

title: Signature Transparency reports
description: Signature edition: Publish what telemetry exists, what it showed, and how privacy was protected — regular transparency reports build the trust that makes telemetry sustainable. What's collected, what's learned, what's spent: the public accounting of the private system.
method: Report collection, findings, and privacy spend regularly; make reports specific enough to verify.
usage: Publish on schedule; specificity is what makes reports credible.

demo.code:
print('Q3 telemetry report: 12 fields, eps spend 2.1, top finding: crash SIG-8812')
print('published: 2026-10-01 (verifiable claims)')

title: Signature Opt-in and consent telemetry
description: Signature edition: The non-cryptographic foundation: telemetry is opt-in, consent is granular (crash reports yes, usage stats no), and users can inspect what's sent. No privacy mechanism substitutes for consent — the best systems combine honest consent UX with strong technical privacy.
method: Opt-in by default-off (or clear opt-out where appropriate); granular toggles; inspectable payloads; honor signals (GPC).
usage: Make consent real (not dark patterns); let users see exactly what's collected.

demo.code:
print('telemetry settings: [x] crash reports [ ] usage stats [ ] performance')
print('user inspects payload: {"crash": "SIG-8812", "os": "android-14"}')

title: Signature Heavy-hitter discovery (private)
description: Signature edition: Which crashes, URLs, or queries are most common? Private heavy-hitter protocols (TrieHH, Apple's) find the top-k frequent items under local DP without learning anyone's individual value. Telemetry's core question — 'what's breaking most?' — answered privately.
method: Hierarchical search over the item space with local-DP votes per level; prune rare prefixes; report heavy hitters with noisy counts.
usage: Use for crash/error triage; the hierarchy bounds the search cost.

demo.code:
print('private heavy hitters: crash SIG-8812 (~12%), ANR-main (~8%)')
print('(noisy counts; individual devices: deniable)')

title: Signature Private quantiles and histograms
description: Signature edition: Latency distributions, not just means: private histograms add Laplace noise per bucket, and private quantiles use the exponential mechanism over candidate values. 'p99 latency rose to 800ms' — learned from millions of devices, none identified.
method: Bucket the metric; add Laplace noise per bucket; derive quantiles; the noise hides individuals, the shape survives.
usage: Size buckets for your metric's range; more buckets = more noise total (budget split).
